info.title: PostureRMM Integration API
info.description:
Access to a PostureRMM install, for scripts and integrations: reads, and the writes that pass the same server-side gates as the web UI.

Within v1 a release may only add: an operation, an optional input, a response field or an enum value. Clients ignore fields they do not know and treat an enum value they do not know as unknown. Lists answer in a `{data, pagination}` envelope; `page` is 1-indexed and `per_page` is clamped to 1-100. The fleet-wide lists (`GET /compliance-results`, `GET /vulnerabilities`) page by `cursor` instead: pass `pagination.next_cursor` back until it is `null`; `per_page` is 1-1000 and there is no total. Every error is `{error, message, details?}`.

put.summary: Turn Auto pre-cache on or off.
put.description:
Super admin only. Off freezes the cache: the feed sync recommends and
fetches nothing new and the daily eviction deletes nothing. It blocks
nothing: Retry, Allow again and an on-demand fetch for a deployment still
work, and an offline install is unaffected. Takes effect at the next sync.
Audited as a settings update, the same row the Bastion page writes.

post.summary: Drain the egress queue now.
post.description:
Super admin only. Clears the retry wait of every queued fetch and tries the
queue at once, for an operator who has just restored egress and should not
wait for a schedule widened while nobody watched. Offline is an answer, not
an error: with the Bastion closed the pass stops early (`door_looks_shut`),
the queue stays durable, and the widened schedule resumes.

200.description: The queue was released; see pass and the counts

post.summary: Remove an app from the cache and exclude it.
post.description:
Super admin only. Deletes the app's cached installer and stops cache-policy
recommending it. It does not stop the app being deployed: an excluded app
that is deployed later still has its installer fetched on demand, and queued
durably while the Bastion is closed. Answers `409`, naming what holds the
installer, while a queued install, a pinned update or an uploaded package
needs it; nothing changes then.

next sync fetches them.

post.summary: Pull the feed now, outside the hourly schedule.
post.description:
Super admin only: the pull writes every shared feed table, for every
Organization (ADR-0072). It answers 202 with no body, and the sync runs
detached in this server process. It is not queued durably: a restart before it
finishes drops it (the next scheduled pull runs regardless), and its outcome is
not returned, only logged and shown on System health, Bastion. A large backlog takes
minutes, which is why the request does not wait. Answers 409 when a pull is
already running (the hourly one, or an earlier Sync Now), and 503 when the
server's feed puller is not running.

post.summary: Dispatch work to endpoints.
post.description:
Admin only. `kind` picks the body: `patch`, `app_install`, `win_update` and
`app_uninstall` answer with what was created; `cart` answers with an
`outcome`. A group-scoped key may name only endpoints in its groups (`403`
otherwise), and nothing is written for a refused request.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` (1 to 200 characters) to make a retry safe. A
repeat with the same key from the same API key or user, within 60 seconds of
the first call that dispatched, answers that call's response (the same
change id, with an `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header) and dispatches
nothing; `422` when the repeat's body is a different request, `409` while the
first call is still running. A call that dispatched nothing (a refusal, an
empty result, a cart awaiting `confirm_dangerous`) does not hold the key.

key).

`password`, or a `code` for an account with TOTP enrolled. Every reveal is
audited (`secret_escrow_reveal`, with the reason, never the value) before the
value is returned, and if that audit row cannot be written nothing is
returned. A wrong password or code is audited
(`secret_escrow_reveal_failure`) and counts toward the account's lockout:
once it trips, the reveal answers 423 until the lockout ends. A wrong guess
answers 401; a missing, overlong or password-repeating `reason` answers 400
and costs no guess.

Revealing a local administrator password retires it: it is rotated at the
endpoint's next check-in (`rotates` says so). A recovery key is not.

401.description: The password or code is wrong. The guess counts toward lockout

Admin only. `action_key` is `posture:` and the id of a Performance rule that

endpoint's `GET /api/v1/endpoints/{id}/tasks`. Each dispatch is audited.

post.summary: Reveal a stored credential's secret.
post.description:
Admin or super admin, and only for the credential's owner: a credential
belongs to the user who created it, so another admin, even a super admin,
answers 404.

**This is a reveal.** It needs a step-up: a `reason` and the caller's
`password`, or a `code` for an account with TOTP enrolled. Every reveal is
audited (`stored_credential_reveal`, with the reason, never the secret)
before the plaintext is returned, and if that audit row cannot be written the
reveal fails and nothing is returned. A wrong password or code is audited
(`stored_credential_reveal_failure`) and counts toward the account's lockout:
once it trips, the reveal answers 423 until the lockout ends. A wrong guess
answers 401; a missing, overlong or password-repeating `reason` answers 400
and costs no guess.

A password credential answers `password`; a private-key credential answers
`secret_kind: "private_key"` and `secret`, with no `password`.

endpoints of your Organization, inside your groups. For one endpoint, with

ComplianceSummaryResponse.description:
Compliance summary response.

**Contract change, 2026-07-25 (#2591).** `total_checks`, `not_applicable`,
`skipped` and the matching `by_status` entries narrowed to *checks that could
apply to this endpoint*: a check written for an operating system this host can
never be no longer appears in any of them. On a Windows 10 endpoint that took
`total_checks` from 2311 to ~679 and `not_applicable` from ~1942 to
approximately zero — the field now means "genuine per-endpoint exception" (a
release-gated check, an absent app) rather than "the rest of the catalog".
`passed`, `failed`, `errors`, `critical_failures`, `high_failures` and
`compliance_percent` are unchanged for every endpoint; the percentage is
`passed / (passed + failed)` and already excluded `not_applicable`. There were
no external consumers pre-launch, so no compatibility shim exists. Rationale
and the paired `compliance_snapshots` step change: ADR-0027 →
"Per-endpoint compliance summary — applicability".

- `compliance_below`: `threshold_percent` (0 to 100; default 80).
- `disk_above`: `threshold_percent` (0 to 100; default 90).
- `critical_cve`: `min_cvss` (0 to 10; default 9).
- `cpu_above`, `memory_above`: `threshold_percent` (0 to 100; default 75),

- `uptime_above`, `certificate_expiring`: `threshold_days` (1 or more;

  systemd unit; required), `require_automatic` (also fail while it would
  not start by itself; default false).
- `process`: `name` (as the Processes view shows it; required),
  `fail_when` (`not_running`, the default, or `running`).
- `event_log`: `channel` (`application`, `system` or `security`;
  required), `levels` (`critical`, `error`, `warning`, `information`,
  `verbose`; empty is every level), `sources` and `event_ids` (at most 20
  each; empty is any), `message_contains`, `threshold` (1 to 1000;
  default 1), `window_minutes` (1 to 10080; default 5).
- `ping`: `host` (required, one word), `max_latency_ms` (1 to 60000;
  default no limit).
- `tcp`: `host` and `port` (1 to 65535; both required), `max_latency_ms`.
- `http`: `url` (`http://` or `https://`; required), `expected_status`
  (codes 100 to 599; empty is any 2xx), `body_contains`,
  `max_latency_ms`, `cert_expiry_days` (1 to 3650, `https` only).
- `script`: `script_id` (an approved library script; required),
  `timeout_secs` (1 to 120; default 60), `exit_codes` (empty is 0 only),
  `stdout_matches` and `stdout_not_matches` (regular expressions of at
  most 256 bytes).

`snmp` belongs to a network device and is refused. The check is saved in
the dialog's normal form: text trimmed, defaults filled in.

InvitationLink.description:
A one-time setup link for an invited user. It is a **credential**: whoever
opens it chooses the account's password. It appears in the response that
minted it and in no other: no read returns it, and a lost link is replaced,
not recovered. The install sends no email; pass the link on out of band.

expires_at.description: The link works once, until this moment. Replacing or revoking it ends it sooner.

invitation_url.description:
**Shown only in this response.** The invitee's setup page. An absolute URL
when the install has a public URL configured, otherwise the path alone
(`/invitations/<token>`) for you to put on the install's address.

InviteUserRequest.description: Request body for inviting a user: no password, the invitee chooses it.

email.description: A valid address. Stored lower-case, and unique across the install.

oneOf.description: Default: `helpdesk`.

scope_group_ids.description:
Group scope for group-scoped roles (Admin, Operator, Helpdesk): each must
be a group of the acting Organization (400 otherwise). Ignored for global
roles (SuperAdmin, Auditor).

InvitedUserResponse.description: A user invited, and the link that lets them in.

user.description: The new user: inactive, with no password, until the link is used.

KeyListItem.description: An install key's metadata. The key value is never served again.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339, or null when the key never expires.

is_expired.description: True when `expires_at` is set and past.

key_prefix.description: `frt_` + four hex characters. There is no full value to serve (#3563).

tag_names.description:
Comma-joined names of tags this key applies to new endpoints it
auto-enrolls (ADR-0070 placement metadata, #1853). Empty when the
key carries no tags.

KillProcessRequest.description: Which process to end, as it is named in the audit log.

name.description:
The process name as the process list shows it. The agent checks it
against the process holding `pid` before it ends it.

LedgerEventResponse.description: One change to the Posture Score, in the caller's points ledger.

points_delta.description:
Points gained (positive) or lost (negative). 0 for an event that moved
nothing, such as the start of an automated fix.

LedgerVerifyResponse.description: Whether the ledger's hash chain is intact.

first_bad_row_id.description: The first row that does not match. Absent when `ok`.

ok.description: False when a row's hash does not match: the ledger was altered.

LicenseResponse.description: The install's license and how much of its endpoint cap is used.

active_count.description: Endpoints counting against the cap, across the whole install.

cap.description: The effective endpoint cap. Null means unlimited.

expiry.description:
The expiry date of the signed license, RFC 3339. Null when the install
holds no license, which is every install today.

is_current.description: True when `last_verified_at` is within the last 7 days.

last_verified_at.description:
When the Bastion last verified the license, RFC 3339. Null when it never
has: normal on a Community install with no license key.

max_endpoints.description:
The licensed endpoint count. Null means unlimited, or that no license
sets one.

paid_feeds.description:
Whether the install's license includes the licensed vulnerability feeds.
The only capability a tier gates: the endpoint cap is the tier boundary,
and every self-hosted feature is in Community (ADR-0019).

pending_count.description:
Endpoints held out of management because the cap is reached
(`pending_community_cap`).

remaining.description:
Slots left before the cap is reached. Null means unlimited; negative when
the cap was lowered below the endpoints already counted.

status.description:
The Bastion's status word for the license (for example `active`,
`expired`). Display text; the tier is what the install acts on.

tier.description:
`community`, the free tier with every feature, which is what every
install reports today. A signed license, when the install holds one, can
set `business` (an older Bastion may report `pro`, which means the
same); a license past its expiry date plus 7 days reads `community`.

LicenseSyncOutcome.description: What a license sync decided about the token the Bastion answered with.

LicenseSyncResponse.description: A license sync that reached the Bastion.

outcome.description:
What the sync decided. Only `in_expiry`, `in_grace`, `post_grace_degrade`
and `community_fallback` mean the install's license is what the Bastion
said; the other two kept the last-known license.

LineAppResponse.description: The app an app line names.

catalog_id.description: The catalog app's id. Null for one of the Organization's own apps.

custom_winget_id.description: The Organization's own app, by `winget_id`. Null for a catalog app.

publisher.description: Empty for an app of the Organization's own.

LocalAccountsResponse.description:
Local accounts and groups. The rows are the agent's own objects.

A user row carries `name`, `full_name`, `sid`, `is_enabled`, `password_expires`
and `account_expires` on both platforms. A Windows agent adds `description`,
`last_logon`, `password_required`, `password_changeable_date`,
`user_may_change_password`, `source` and `object_class`; a Linux agent adds
`uid` and sends a null `sid`. A group row carries `name`, `sid` and `members`
(names), plus `description` and `source` on Windows or `gid` on Linux. The
rows are not part of the v1 promise beyond the fields named here.

A Linux agent that cannot read its account files answers `200` with
`{"error": "..."}` and neither list.

days_of_week.description: The days it opens on, `0` (Sunday) to `6` (Saturday).

end_time.description:
When it closes, `HH:MM` in `timezone`. Earlier than `start_time` means
it closes the next morning.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it covers.

group_ids.description:
The groups it covers. With no endpoints either, it covers the whole
Organization.

source_revision.description:
Set when this window is a linked copy of another Organization's window:
the source revision it carries. A copy's name, days, times and zone are
its source's and are read-only until it is detached; its targets and
`enabled` stay its own.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name, for example `Europe/London`.

ManageStartupItemRequest.description: The startup item to change, as the startup-item list names it.

item_type.description:
The item's `item_type`: `run_key_hklm`, `run_key_hkcu`, `run_once_key_hklm`,
`run_once_key_hkcu`, `startup_folder_allusers`, `startup_folder_user`,
`scheduled_task`, `systemd_unit`, `cron_reboot` or `rc_local`. Any other
value answers `400`.

source_path.description:
The item's `source_path`: a registry key, a folder, a scheduled task's
full path or a file.

weight.description: How much the control counts toward the mandate's coverage.

MandateDetailResponse.description: One mandate with every control's coverage.

MandateMeasureResponse.description: The checks a control cites, and how they stand on this fleet.

checks_assessed.description: How many of them reached a verdict on this fleet.

prc_ids.description: The check ids the control cites.

MandateSummaryResponse.description: One mandate's coverage on this fleet.

body.description: The body that publishes the mandate.

controls_not_assessed.description: Controls nothing could be assessed against. They are not failures.

coverage_percent.description:
0 to 100, weighted over the assessed controls only. Null when nothing
could be assessed: 0 is a measurement and this is not one.

slug.description: Stable identifier; the path parameter of the detail read.

MessageDeliveries.description: One page of a message's notifications, in the list envelope.

delivered_at.description: When the agent reported the notification shown. Null until it does.

task_id.description:
The task that carries the notification to the agent
(`GET /api/v1/endpoints/{id}/tasks/{task_id}`). Null once the task is
pruned.

deliveries.description: One page of the endpoints the message was queued for, by hostname.

MessageDetail.description: A message and each endpoint's notification, by hostname.

MessageSummary.description: A sent message and how it landed.

created_by.description: The user who sent it. Null once that user is deleted.

target.description:
How the sender chose the recipients. Treat a value you do not know as
`all`.

target_ids.description:
The ids the sender named: groups or endpoints, by `target`. Empty for
`all`.

disk_usage.description:
Volumes as the agent reported them. Always an empty array in the
downsampled ranges (`24h`, `7d`, `30d`). Free-form: the volume keys are
not part of the v1 promise.

recorded_at.description: The reading's time; the start of its bucket in a downsampled range.

ModeWire.description: What a drift on an assigned device gets.

MonitorResponse.description: A custom monitor and the alert it raises.

channel_ids.description: Notification channels the alert is delivered through.

check.description:
What each endpoint checks: `{"kind": "<kind>", "config": {…}}`, as
`POST /monitors` describes it. A script monitor is stored without its
script body.

cooldown_minutes.description: Minutes before the alert may fire again for the same endpoint.

endpoint_ids.description: Endpoints the monitor covers in addition to its groups.

group_ids.description:
Groups the monitor covers. With `endpoint_ids`, empty is the whole
Organization.

muted.description: True while a mute is in effect.

muted_until.description: When the mute ends. Null for a monitor that is not muted.

revision.description:
Moves each time the check changes, so results measured under the old one
stop counting.

MspLeaderboardResponse.description: The Organizations ranked by Posture Score.

rows.description: Highest score first, ties by name; Organizations without a score come last.

MspLeaderboardRowResponse.description:
One Organization on the leaderboard. Every figure is null while the
Organization has no stateable score.

current_score.description:
The Organization's latest stored Posture Score, 0 to 1000. Null when the
newest snapshot is missing a pillar (ADR-0027 withholds the composite
until all three have measured), when there is no snapshot, and for a key
limited to some groups of its home Organization.

delta_7d.description:
`current_score` minus the stored score 6 to 8 days back. Null whenever
`current_score` is, and when there is no snapshot in that span.

grade.description: A letter band of `current_score`. Null with it.

stale_snapshot_age_days.description:
Days since the newest snapshot, even when its score is withheld. Null
when there has never been one.

MspOverviewResponse.description: Totals across the Organizations the caller manages.

avg_compliance.description:
Mean of the Organizations' `compliance_percent`, weighted by endpoint
count, one decimal. Not the Posture Score: see `compliance_percent` on
the per-Organization summary.

MspTenantSummaryResponse.description: One Organization's card on the MSP dashboard.

compliance_percent.description:
Mean of the compliance summaries of the Organization's endpoints seen in
the last 24 hours and scanned in the last 7 days, one decimal. Each
summary is pass over pass and fail across every profile's applicable
checks. It is not the Posture Score: the Prevention pillar counts only
the PostureRMM Recommended profile (ADR-0034), and the score is on the
leaderboard. 0 when no endpoint qualifies.

NameMatchWire.description: How a name rule compares the display name.

pid.description:
The owning process. Null where no owner is visible, for example a
`TIME_WAIT` socket.

remote_address.description: `address:port`. An unconnected socket shows its wildcard.

state.description: A netstat-style state such as `ESTABLISHED` or `LISTENING`.

NetworkConnectionsResponse.description:
Open sockets on the endpoint.

A Linux agent that cannot read its socket tables answers `200` with
`{"error": "..."}` and no `connections`.

discovered_device_id.description: The discovered device it was added from. Null once that one is deleted.

expected_down_ports.description: Every port marked expected down, reported or not. Empty in a list.

oneOf.description: Null until a probe has read the device's system group.

ports.description:
The ports the device last reported. Empty in a list: read the device for
them.

probe_endpoint_id.description:
The endpoint that pings it. Null until chosen, or once that endpoint is
deleted; nothing is monitored without one.

secret.description:
The new secret. **Shown only in this response**: store it now. The old
one is refused from this moment.

NoPayloadReasonWire.description:
Why a Windows Update was left out of a dispatch. Treat an unknown value as
unknown.

NonReportingEndpointResponse.description: An endpoint that has not reported for a day.

hours_offline.description: Whole hours since the endpoint last reported. 9999 when it never has.

NotifyEndpointRequest.description: A message to show the signed-in user.

admin_password.description: The first administrator's password, a secret.

install_key_name.description: Also issue an install key with this name.

oneOf.description: Null unless `install_key_name` was sent.

msp_grant_created.description: Whether the caller was granted access to the Organization.

key.description: The full install key. A secret, shown only in this response and never again.

PackageSkipReasonWire.description:
Why a Linux package pair was not dispatched: the string `not_applicable`,
`not_linux` or `already_in_flight`, or `{"undeliverable": <reason>}`. Treat an unknown value
as unknown.

PatchBaselineResponse.description: A patch baseline and its lines.

PatchBaselineSummary.description: A patch baseline in a list, without its lines.

pinned_apps.description: App lines held at a version ceiling.

PatchFreezeResponse.description: Whether a fleet-wide patch freeze is in effect.

active.description:
True when `windows` is not empty. A posture action's `do` is refused
while it is.

windows.description:
The enabled windows that cover the whole Organization (no group, no
endpoint target) and contain the current UTC time and weekday.

deferral_days.description: Days an endpoint may defer an update the rules do not decide, `0` to `90`.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it covers.

group_ids.description:
The groups it covers. With no endpoints either, it covers the whole
Organization.

source_revision.description:
Set when this policy is a linked copy of another Organization's policy:
the source revision it carries. A copy's name, description, rules and
deferral are its source's and are read-only until it is detached; its
targets and `enabled` stay its own.

PatchPostureActionRequest.description:
A change to an action. A field left out stays as it is; the fields that can
be cleared also take an explicit `null`.

owner_user_id.description: The user who owns the action. `null` removes the owner.

risk_accept_expires.description: The day an accepted risk lapses. `null` accepts it indefinitely.

risk_accept_reason.description: Why the risk is accepted. It is audited with the acceptance.

PatchRuleRequest.description: One rule of a patch policy, as it is written. Rules are read in order.

oneOf.description: Absent or null matches any classification.
Absent or null matches any severity.

PatchRuleResponse.description: One rule of a patch policy, as it is stored.

severity.description:
`critical`, `important`, `moderate`, `low` or `unspecified`; null matches
any. A rule stored by hand before this API existed can carry another
spelling, which is reported as stored.

PatchSummaryResponse.description: Counts of an endpoint's Windows updates by state.

critical.description: Severity breakdown of the missing and approved updates.

last_scan_at.description: The most recent scan across the endpoint's update rows.

not_applicable.description:
Updates an authoritative scan stopped reporting missing without
reporting them installed.

PeerBaselineResponse.description:
Percentile scores for a category and industry cohort, delivered by the feed.
They are not computed from this install's fleet.

as_of.description: The day the percentiles were computed.

granted_by.description:
The administrator who granted it. Null for a `group` grant, or when that
administrator was since removed.

group.description: The SSO group, for a `group` grant.

PermissionStateResponse.description: Whether one add-on permission is held, and every grant behind it.

grantable.description: The role can hold it at all. An auditor, being read-only, cannot.

grants.description:
Every grant, oldest first. A grant left behind by a change to a role that
cannot hold it is listed but does not make `held` true.

held.description: The user holds it: through the role, or through any grant their role may hold.

in_role.description: The role includes it (Admin, super admin): there is nothing to grant.

PermissionWire.description: An add-on permission a user holds beside their role. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

PhysicalDisk.description: One physical disk and its SMART state.

device_id.description: Unique per host on Windows. Absent on Linux and from older agents.

nvme_percentage_used.description: NVMe percentage of rated life consumed, 0-100. Absent for other disks.

read_errors_uncorrected.description: Absent when the disk does not report it.

temperature_celsius.description: Degrees Celsius. Absent when the disk does not report it.

write_errors_uncorrected.description: Absent when the disk does not report it.

coverage_pct.description: Share of the pillar's rules that were measured, 0.0 to 1.0.

score_pct.description:
0.0 to 1.0. Null when the pillar measured nothing (`coverage_pct` is 0):
that is "not yet measured", never a score of zero.

PillarWeightsResponse.description: How much each pillar counts toward the Posture Score.

PinResponse.description: A profile version the Organization pinned.

pinned_by.description: The user who pinned it; null once that user is gone.

PortMarkResponse.description: The port as it now stands.

name.description: The name the device reports for it, or the name it was marked with.

expected_down.description: Marked expected down: the Interfaces check leaves it out.

speed_bps.description: Bits per second; null when the device reports none.

PortStateWire.description:
A port's admin or operational state (RFC 2863). Treat an unknown value as
unknown.

PostureActionResponse.description:
One recommended action: a fix that raises the Posture Score, and where it
stands in the risk register.

action_key.description:
Stable key of the finding, for example `compliance:<check id>` or
`patch:CVE-2026-0001`.

affected_count.description: Endpoints the finding is open on.

auto_action_type.description:
`deploy` (install an app from the catalog) or `script`. Null when the
action has no automatic fix.

auto_fixable.description: The action carries an automatic fix: `do` can run it.

auto_source_id.description: The catalog entry or script the fix runs.

category.description:
`patching`, `vulnerabilities`, `compliance`, `hardening`, `operations` or
`deploy_software`. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

freeze_hold.description:
A patch freeze window that covers the whole Organization is in effect now,
and the action is a patching, vulnerabilities or hardening one.

gain_points.description:
Points of the Posture Score (on the dashboard's 0 to 100) that completing
the action recovers. Frozen while the risk is accepted.

last_seen_at.description:
When the generator last changed this action's content (title, gain,
affected count, effort, impact, auto-fix) or reopened it. An unchanged
action keeps its value across passes, so it is not a "still seen" time.

risk_accept_expires.description:
The day an accepted risk lapses and the points come back. Null for an
indefinite acceptance, and for an action whose risk is not accepted.

PostureActionsResponse.description: The recommended actions that match the filter, open ones first.

actions.description: Open first, then by points recovered, largest first.

total_gain_open.description: The points all open actions would recover, whatever the filter.

total_open.description: Every open action in the Organization, whatever the filter.

PostureBaselineResponse.description: The scored baseline Prevention was computed under (ADR-0112).

coverage_pct.description: How much of what applies to the fleet the pillar measured, 0 to 1.

critical_fail_triggered.description:
A rule flagged critical-fail has a confirmed failure. A flag, not a cap:
it does not move the score.

score_pct.description: The pillar's score over what it measured, 0 to 1.

PostureExplodeResponse.description:
The Posture Score with every rule under it: the same composite as
`posture-score`, one level deeper.

PostureParameter.description: A threshold of a Performance rule, and where this Organization has set it.

default_value.description: What the rule uses until the Organization overrides it.

effective_value.description:
`override_value`, or `default_value` when there is none: what the rule
uses.

group_name.description: Display heading of the rule file this rule belongs to.

override_value.description: The Organization's own value. Null while it follows the default.

PostureParametersResponse.description: Every threshold the Organization can tune.

PostureScoreResponse.description:
The fleet's Posture Score: the composite of the three pillars, Prevention,
Patching and Performance (ADR-0027), with its movement.

grade.description:
A letter band of the composite. Null while `measured` is false: nothing
has been graded, and a client must not show an `F` for it.

measured.description:
False while a pillar has measured nothing. `score`, `score_pct` and `grade`
are then a mean over the pillars that did, and a client must not present
them as the fleet's number (ADR-0027).

ruleset_version.description:
The ruleset the rules were evaluated under. A change of ruleset moves the
score without the fleet having changed.

score.description: The composite on the legacy 0 to 1000 scale.

score_pct.description: The composite, 0 to 1. Prefer it to `score`.

today_delta.description:
`score` minus the stored snapshot's score of the day before, for the
same groups: a key limited to some groups is compared with the snapshot
stored for those groups (ADR-0173). Null when that day has no measured
snapshot, as for groups not yet snapshotted then, and when the
Prevention baseline changed since (ADR-0112).

unavailable_pts.description: `round((1 - coverage_pct) x 1000)`: the points nothing has measured yet.

PostureTargetResponse.description: The Posture Score the Organization aims for.

set_by.description: The user who set it. Null when unset, or once that user is gone.

target.description: On the 0 to 1000 scale of `score`. 850 until someone sets one.

PostureTrendPointResponse.description: One day of the fleet posture series.

PostureTrendResponse.description: The fleet composite over a window, one point per snapshot day.

points.description:
Oldest first. A day on which a pillar measured nothing has no point. A
key limited to some groups gets the series stored for those groups
(ADR-0173), which starts the day they were first snapshotted.

window.description: The window that was applied: `7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `90d` or `1y`.

PreviewRequest.description: What a list of banned applications would match today.

disk_read_bytes_per_sec.description: Bytes read from disk since the last sample (a delta, not a total).

disk_written_bytes_per_sec.description: Bytes written to disk since the last sample (a delta, not a total).

start_time_unix.description: Start time as Unix epoch seconds.

ProfileSummaryResponse.description: A compliance profile and how the fleet stands against it.

applicable_hosts.description:
Endpoints this profile's platform can apply to. Null means the platform
applicability registry has not reached this install: it is not zero.

compliance_percent.description:
0 to 100, one decimal: passing rules over the rules that reached a verdict
(pass, fail, error). An error is not a pass; a failure under an accepted
risk counts as passing.

excepted.description: The part of `failed` and `errored` under a live accepted risk.

id.description: Database id of the profile row.

last_assessed.description: The newest result for this profile in the key's scope.

not_measured.description:
Rules with no verdict yet: never scanned, withheld from the agent, or
skipped.

pinned_version.description: Version the Organization pinned, null when it follows the latest.

oneOf.description:
The qualified verdict for a published benchmark; null for anything else
(the scored baseline, a framework lens, a PostureRMM-authored profile),
which has none.

PropertyDefinitionRequest.description: A definition to create, or the whole of what one is replaced with.

description.description: Omit it for none; on a replace that clears it.

display_order.description: Where it sorts, lowest first. Defaults to `0`.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters. Unique in the Organization.

params.description: What the agent reads, as stored: the keys `property_type` names.

visible_by_default.description: Whether the console shows it on an endpoint without being asked.

PropertyParams.description:
The boxes a collection method reads. Send the ones `property_type` names, and
leave the rest out.

namespace.description:
The WMI namespace: `root\CIMv2` and the other read-only system namespaces
the console offers. Any other is refused.

path.description: A file's path (`file_*`) or a registry key's path (`registry_*`).

value_name.description: The registry value to read. Without one, the key's default value.

PropertyValueResponse.description: The value of one custom property on one endpoint.

property_type.description:
How the agent collects it: `file_version`, `file_exists`, `file_hash`,
`registry_value`, `registry_exists`, `environment_variable` or
`wmi_query`. Treat a value you do not know as unknown.

value.description: Null until collected, or when collection failed.

total.description:
Every relay the install knows. Relays belong to the install, not to an
Organization or a group.

tls_ca_fingerprint.description:
SHA-256 of the CA the proxy's TLS listener chains to, from its last
heartbeat: what the agents behind it pin. Null when it reports none.

ProxyResponse.description:
One proxy. There is no secret here: it is shown when the proxy is created or
re-keyed, and never again.

ProxyStatus.description:
Whether the proxy has reported in lately. Treat a value you do not know as
unknown.

ProxySummary.description:
One proxy in a list. There is no secret here: it is shown when the proxy is
created or re-keyed, and never again.

connected_agents.description: Endpoints whose agents last reached the server through this proxy.

last_heartbeat.description: The proxy's last heartbeat. RFC 3339. Null when it has never reported.

version.description: The proxy software's version, from its last heartbeat.

ProxyWithSecret.description: A proxy and its new secret.

backend_ca_pin.description:
The server's CA fingerprint, for `POSTURERMM_PROXY_BACKEND_CA_PIN` in the
proxy's environment. Null when the server's certificate is one the proxy
already trusts, which needs no pin.

secret.description:
The proxy's secret, 64 hex characters. **Shown only in this response**:
store it now. The proxy sends it with its id on every heartbeat.

reason.description: Why the PSA could not be reached, for `unreachable`.

truncated.description:
The PSA holds more companies than this list carries; the first ones by
name are listed. An id outside it can still be set.

company_id.description: The company's id in the PSA.

company_name.description: The PSA's name for the company. Null while the id is unconfirmed.

confirmed.description: Whether the PSA itself vouched for the id when it was saved.

mapped.description: `false` when the Organization has no mapping; the other fields are then null.

PsaConnectionState.description: Whether the PSA could be asked for its companies.

PutBody.description: The Posture Score to aim for.

target.description:
On the 0 to 1000 scale of the Posture Score's `score`. Anything outside
that answers `400`.

PutBrand.description:
The brand text to change. A field left out keeps its value; an empty string
clears it, so PostureRMM's own shows.

name.description: Up to 60 characters, on one line.

warn_after_days.description: Whole days, 1 to 3650. Outside that answers `422`.

PutDetection.description: How endpoints running the app are recognized.

oneOf.description: `name`: how `pattern` is compared. Default `equals`.

pattern.description:
`name`: the name the app shows in Installed apps. A start or fragment
needs at least 3 characters.

product_code.description:
`msi`: the ProductCode, with or without braces. Give this, the
UpgradeCode, or both.

upgrade_code.description: `msi`: the UpgradeCode, which stays the same across versions.

PutHealthBands.description: The cut-points to set. A bound left out keeps its value.

critical_max.description: Critical below this score. 0 to 100, below `healthy_min`.

healthy_min.description: Healthy from this score up. 0 to 100, above `critical_max`.

PutParameter.description: One threshold to set or clear.

override_value.description:
The value to write. `null` clears the override, so the rule follows its
default again. A value outside the parameter's `min` and `max` answers
`400`.

PutPillarWeights.description: The weights to set. A pillar left out keeps its weight.

patching.description: Patching's weight. Finite and not negative.

performance.description: Performance's weight. Finite and not negative.

prevention.description: Prevention's weight. Finite and not negative.

PutRetention.description: The retention settings to change. A field left out keeps its value.

silent_args.description:
Replaces the arguments the version was uploaded with at every install.
Null, or blank, clears the override.

RawTelemetryResponse.description: The most recent check-in the endpoint's agent sent, credentials removed.

payload.description:
The check-in as the agent sent it, except that `performance_samples` and
`task_results` are replaced by their lengths, `performance_samples_count`
and `task_results_count`. Free-form: its keys follow the agent's version
and are not part of the v1 promise. Null when `received_at` is.

received_at.description: Null when the agent has not checked in.

ReachabilitySample.description: One 30-minute bucket of the 24-hour reachability series.

ratio.description: Fraction of samples that were reachable, 0.0 to 1.0.

rtt.description: Average heartbeat round trip in ms; null when the bucket measured none.

ReattachCandidate.description: The admitted endpoint a waiting request claims to be.

RebootIndicatorsResponse.description:
Which pending-reboot indicators the agent observed. A `false` means not
observed; `unreadable` names the indicators the agent could not read.

deadline_hours.description: How long an endpoint may put off a required restart, 1 to 168 hours.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it covers.

grace_period_minutes.description: The warning the signed-in user gets before a restart, 0 to 1440 minutes.

group_ids.description:
The groups it covers. With no endpoints either, it covers the whole
Organization.

RecommendedBinaryDto.description: One app the cache holds or wants, or one the operator excluded.

excluded_by.description: Who excluded it, for an `excluded` row.

last_pull_error.description: Why the last fetch failed, as stored.

version.description: Empty for an excluded app, which has no recommendation.

winget_id.description: The winget id, which is what Remove and Allow again name.

RecommendedBinaryList.description: Every recommended binary, and every excluded app.

ReconciliationLogEntry.description: What one feed sync retired from the catalog.

apps_removed.description: Apps the feed dropped from the catalog.

bundle_version.description: The feed bundle version the sync applied. Null when it carried none.

packages_superseded.description: Patch packages replaced by a newer one.

ReinstateResponse.description: The outcome of reinstating a decommissioned endpoint.

status.description:
Always `pending`: the endpoint is `online` again once its agent next
checks in.

reason.description:
Up to 500 characters. Recorded on the script. Defaults to the console's
"Rejected by an administrator."

oneOf.description:
One deployment fanned out across `dispatched` targets (`queued` of which
were offline and apply at next check-in).

Dangerous remediation withheld pending `confirm_dangerous=true`. Nothing
was dispatched; send the request again with the flag to apply it.

RemediateActionResponse.description:
Outcome of a per-row bulk remediate dispatch (ADR-0056 Decision 3).

Mirrors the single-result `RemediateResultResponse` shape so API clients
handle both surfaces uniformly, but carries the device-count blast radius
the bulk confirm needs.

oneOf.description: A deployment+task was created.

Dangerous remediation withheld pending `confirm_dangerous=true`. Nothing
was dispatched; send the request again with the flag to apply it.

RemediateResultResponse.description:
Outcome of a remediate dispatch request (ADR-0056 Decision 3).

`Dispatched` is the existing behaviour; `ConfirmationRequired` is the
server-authoritative guard rail — a structured response (not a dispatch)
the UI renders as the two-step confirm. A fix the gate refuses yields
neither: it answers 422 (see `remediation_gate`).

deployment_id.description: The deployment holding the tasks. Null when nothing was dispatched.

skipped.description: The drifted pairs whose agent cannot run the task, and why.

tasks_created.description: One task per drifted endpoint and feature.

closed.description: Live sessions closed, socket and record both.

failed.description:
Sessions whose socket was closed but whose record failed to write. Never
"sessions still running".

files_deleted.description: Installer files deleted from the cache; 0 when none was cached.

is_template.description:
A shipped template: every Organization sees it, and it can be run and
cloned but not changed or deleted.

ReportFormat.description: The file format of a generated report.

directory_readable.description: `false` when the downloads directory could not be read; the index was left as it was.

indexed.description: Releases written or refreshed in the index.

versions_on_disk.description: Versions of the releases found on disk.

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Request body for admin password reset.

password.description: The new password, a secret. The user must change it at the next sign-in.

ok.description: Always `true`: a failure answers an error body.

audit_log_retention_days.description:
Days audit entries are kept. 0 keeps every entry indefinitely, which is
the default; otherwise 1 to 3650 and older entries are pruned.

compliance_snapshot_retention_days.description: Days compliance snapshots are kept. 30 to 3650. Default 365.

endpoint_auto_delete_enabled.description:
Whether an inactive endpoint is deleted, with all its history. Off by
default.

endpoint_delete_after_days.description:
Days without contact before an inactive endpoint is deleted. 1 to 3650,
more than `endpoint_inactive_after_days`. Default 90.

endpoint_inactive_after_days.description:
Days without a check-in before an endpoint is inactive. 1 to 3650.
Default 7.

endpoint_posture_snapshot_retention_days.description: Days per-endpoint posture snapshots are kept. 30 to 3650. Default 365.

task_retention_days.description: Days task history is kept. 7 to 3650. Default 90.

fetches_started.description:
Fetches started now. Null when the Bastion could not be asked (a closed
maintenance window reads this way): the rows stay pending, durably, and
are fetched on the next sync.

reset.description: Failed rows put back to pending.

RevealSecretRequest.description: Which secret to reveal, and the proof.

code.description:
A current authenticator code. Honoured only for an account with TOTP
enrolled, and then used instead of the password.

password.description: The caller's own password. Needed unless `code` is given.

reason.description:
Why the secret is needed. Up to 500 characters. It is recorded in the
audit log, so it must not repeat the password or code.

subject.description: The secret's `subject` from the endpoint's secrets.

rotates.description:
The value is now retired: a revealed local administrator password is
rotated at the endpoint's next check-in, so the value shown is the last
time it is good. A recovery key is not.

RevertRequest.description:
The acknowledgements a revert may need. Both are optional: send `{}` first and
read what the server asks for.

confirm_count.description:
The number of machines the revert touches, as the server counted them.
Required for a revert of more than one machine, and for a fix that was
verified as working. A number that is not the server's count asks again.

confirm_dangerous.description: Acknowledges a revert that could cut off remote access. Default false.

oneOf.description: The revert was dispatched as a new Change.

deployment_ids.description: The new Change that undoes the fixes.

oneOf.description:
Nothing was dispatched. Send the request again with `confirm_count` set to
`expected_count`.

expected_count.description: The number of machines the revert touches.

why.description: Why the count is asked for. Human-readable; may change between releases.

oneOf.description:
Nothing was dispatched. Undoing the fix could break remote access: send the
request again with `confirm_dangerous: true` once you have another way in.

hazard.description: What could break. Human-readable; may change between releases.

RevertResponse.description: What a revert request answered. `outcome` says which.

RiskAcceptanceResponse.description:
Why a rule's risk is accepted. An accepted rule scores as a pass for as long
as the acceptance lasts (ADR-0027).

expires.description: The day the acceptance lapses. Null is an indefinite acceptance.

RoleWire.description: What a user or an API key may do. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

RolloutRequest.description: Which endpoints a rollout reaches, and how many.

count.description: How many endpoints, for `scope` `count`. At least 1.

scope.description:
`all` (every active endpoint), `tag` (endpoints carrying `tag_id`) or `count` (the first
`count` endpoints that need the release, most recently seen first). Endpoints already on
or past the release are left out of each.

deployment_id.description: The deployment that tracks the batch. Absent when no endpoint in scope needed the release.

dispatched.description: Upgrade tasks queued. The tasks have not run: read the deployment for progress.

message.description: Why nothing was queued, when nothing was.

target_count.description: Endpoints the batch was sized for.

RotateCredentialRequest.description: A new secret for a credential. The name, username and domain stay as they are.

password.description:
The new secret: a password, or the key text when `secret_kind` is
`private_key`. Also accepted under the name `secret`. Never served again
except by the decrypt operation.

secret_kind.description:
What the new secret is. Defaults to `password`. An `ssh` credential may
rotate to either; every other type takes a password.

enabled.description:
Whether the agents rotate their local administrator's password. Off by
default.

interval_days.description: Days between rotations, 1 to 365. Kept while rotation is off.

RuleAction.description:
What a rule does with an update it matches. An update no rule matches is
left for an operator to decide.

RuleCategory.description: What a rule matches on Windows Update classification.

RuleEndpointsResponse.description: How the endpoints stand against one rule.

rule_id.description: For a Prevention rule, the check's PRC id. Otherwise the dotted id asked for.

rule_name.description: Null when the rule is unknown.

RuleSeverity.description:
What a rule matches on severity. Treat an unknown value as unknown: a rule
stored before this API existed may carry a spelling outside this list.

deployment_ids.description: The deployments created, which are Changes. Empty for `nothing_to_do`.

ScanConfigResponse.description: A scan config: a subnet the backend (or a proxy) scans for devices.

scan_source.description:
Who scans: `backend`, or `proxy:` and the proxy's id for a config a proxy
owns. Treat any other value as unknown.

schedule.description:
A cron expression the scan runs on. Null: manual-only, run it with
`POST /network-scan-configs/{id}/trigger`.

ScanResponse.description:
What a vulnerability scan of one endpoint did. A count of work done, not a
list of findings: read those from the vulnerabilities routes.

The first three counts are the application lane's (CPE matching). On a Linux
endpoint the dpkg and rpm packages are matched against the distribution's
advisories instead, in the same scan, and are not in them: an endpoint with
hundreds of packages can report a handful evaluated. `vulns_created` and
`vulns_auto_resolved` cover every lane.

cpe_unmatched.description:
Applications with no CPE match. They have no CPE vulnerability lane, so
this is the endpoint's application coverage gap.

software_evaluated.description:
Installed applications looked at by CPE matching. Not Linux distribution
packages, which have no CPE (they are matched against advisories).

vulns_auto_resolved.description: Open vulnerabilities this scan found fixed and closed, from every lane.

vulns_created.description:
Vulnerabilities newly recorded, from every lane: applications, Windows
updates and Linux distribution advisories.

ScanRunResponse.description: One execution of a scan config.

devices_found.description: Devices the scan found; 0 until it completes.

status.description: `running`, `completed` or `failed`. Treat any other value as unknown.

trigger.description: `manual` or `scheduled`. Treat any other value as unknown.

ScheduleFrequencyWire.description:
How often a schedule runs. A request names it, a response reports it, so this
mirror reads as well as writes. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

day_of_month.description:
The day of the month a monthly schedule runs. Null for the other
frequencies.

days_of_week.description:
The days a weekly schedule runs, `0` (Sunday) to `6`. Null for the other
frequencies.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it covers.

group_ids.description:
The groups it covers. With no endpoints either, it covers the whole
Organization.

last_run_at.description: When it last ran. Null until it has.

next_run_at.description: When it next runs. Null while it is disabled.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name, for example `Europe/London`.

day_of_month.description:
The day of the month a monthly schedule runs. Null for the other
frequencies.

days_of_week.description:
The days a weekly schedule runs, `0` (Sunday) to `6`. Null for the other
frequencies.

last_error.description: Why the last run failed. Null when it did not.

last_run_at.description: When it last ran. Null until it has.

last_status.description: `success` or `failed`. Null until it has run.

next_run_at.description: When it next runs. Null while it is disabled.

notification_channel_id.description: The notification channel it is emailed through.

timezone.description: An IANA zone name, for example `Europe/London`.

SchedulerHealthResponse.description: What the install's scheduler has been doing.

SchedulerStateWire.description:
What the scheduler's task table says taken as a whole. Treat an unknown value
as unknown.

SchedulerTaskResponse.description: The last run of one scheduled task.

stale.description: The task has not run for longer than it should.

ScriptLanguageWire.description: The interpreter a script runs under. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

ScriptResponse.description: A script in the library, without its code.

approved_at.description: When it was last approved. Null until it is, and cleared by an edit.

rejection_reason.description: Why it was rejected, while it is.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the agent lets it run.

version.description: Counts each edit that changed what the script runs.

ScriptStatusWire.description:
Where a script is in its approval. Only an `approved` script runs. Treat an
unknown value as unknown.

SecretKindWire.description:
What a stored credential's secret is. A request names it, a response reports
it, so this mirror reads as well as writes. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

SectionRequest.description: A section to put in a definition.

filters.description:
`{"severity": "critical,high"}`, a comma-separated list of `critical`,
`high`, `medium`, `low`. No other key is accepted.

title.description: The section's heading. Omit it for the type's own label.

SectionResponse.description: One section of a report definition.

filters.description:
`{"severity": "critical,high"}` on a `compliance_detail` section that is
narrowed to those severities. Null otherwise.

order.description: Its place in the report, from 0.

SelfService.description: Whether end users may apply safe hardening fixes themselves.

hardening_enabled.description:
On: end users are offered the safe fixes for their own machine
(ADR-0117). Off by default.

body.description:
1 to 2000 characters. Line breaks and tabs are kept; no other control
characters.

endpoint_ids.description:
The endpoints to message, for `target` `endpoints`: at least one. Leave
out for any other target.

group_ids.description:
The groups to message, for `target` `groups`: at least one. A dynamic
group's members count. Leave out for any other target.

title.description: One line, 1 to 200 characters, no control characters.

message.description: The recorded message, with its delivery counts.

queued.description:
Notifications queued for an agent that will fetch them at its next
check-in.

sent.description: Notifications pushed to an agent that is connected now.

skipped.description:
Endpoints whose agent cannot show a notification. Nothing was queued for
them.

total.description: Endpoints the target resolved to, skipped ones included.

ServiceActionResponse.description: The agent's answer to a service control or configuration request.

message.description:
Set by a Windows agent that had nothing to do, for example
`already running`.

status.description: `success`. A failure answers `422` with the agent's message instead.

is_microsoft.description:
A vendor-owned service (signed by Microsoft on Windows, a distribution
unit on Linux). Stopping or disabling one needs `confirmation_name`.

name.description: The name to put in the control routes' `{name}`.

oneOf.description: What the service does when it fails. Null where the platform has none.

signer.description: The executable's signer, when its signature is valid.

start_type.description:
`auto`, `auto_delayed`, `manual` or `disabled`. Treat any other value as
unknown.

status.description:
`running`, `stopped`, `paused`, `start_pending`, `stop_pending`,
`continue_pending` or `pause_pending`. Treat any other value as unknown.

ServiceListResponse.description: Services (Windows) or systemd units (Linux) on the endpoint.

ServiceWriteRequest.description: An `is_microsoft` a client still sends is ignored (#5198).

confirmation_name.description:
The service's name, typed back. Required to stop or restart a
vendor-owned service (`is_microsoft` in the service list); the agent's
list, not the request, says which services those are.

enabled.description:
Enabling computes the next run from now; disabling clears it. Setting the
state a policy is already in changes nothing.

SetPasswordRequest.description: The account and its new password.

password.description:
The new password, a secret. The agent checks its strength, and a weak one
fails the task.

password_must_change.description: The user must choose a new password at the next sign-in.

SetPortRequest.description: Mark a port expected down, or clear the mark.

SetProbeRequest.description: The probe to pin a device to.

probe_endpoint_id.description:
The endpoint that pings the device every minute and reports at its
check-in, so it must be on the device's network. Null: no probe, stop
pinging. The key is required, so an empty body cannot clear a probe.

company_id.description: The company's id in the PSA, a whole number above zero.

company_name.description: The PSA's name for the company; null when it could not be asked.

unconfirmed_because.description:
Why the PSA could not confirm the id, when it could not. A later save
confirms it.

interval_days.description: Days between rotations, 1 to 365. Absent keeps the stored interval.

SetSnmpRequest.description:
A device's SNMP settings. The secrets are write-only.

No `Debug`: it holds them.

community.description:
v2c only. At most 255 characters. Left out or blank: the stored string is
kept. A value replaces it. Never returned.

v3_auth_key.description:
v3 only. 8 to 256 characters. Left out or blank: the stored key is kept.
A value replaces it. Never returned.

oneOf.description: v3 only. Left out: the stored one, else `sha256`.

v3_priv_key.description:
v3 only. 8 to 256 characters. Left out or blank: the stored key is kept.
A value replaces it. Never returned.

oneOf.description: v3 only. Left out: the stored one, else `aes128`.

v3_user.description:
v3 only. The USM user name, at most 32 characters. Left out: the stored
one.

version.description: `v3` (recommended) or `v2c`, which sends its community string in clear.

severity.description: `unscored` is its own bucket; `none` counts a real CVSS 0.0 only (#5303).

SilentArgsResponse.description: A package's silent arguments as they now stand.

silent_args.description: The arguments the package carries: the upload's, or the feed's.

silent_args_override.description: The override in force, if any; it replaces `silent_args` at every install.

SkipReasonWire.description: Why a dispatch left an endpoint out. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

SkippedEndpoint.description: An endpoint that was not messaged, and why.

reason.description: Why, for example that its agent is too old to show a notification.

SkippedEndpointDto.description: An endpoint in scope that the release cannot reach.

reason.description: Why: no package for its platform, or an agent that cannot run an upgrade.

SkippedEndpointResponse.description:
An endpoint a dispatch did not create work for, or one endpoint and item pair
it created no work for.

detail.description: Human-readable text. It may change between releases.

oneOf.description: Set when the skip is one endpoint and item pair rather than the endpoint.

Set when the skip is about one user's session on the endpoint (a
user-only app) rather than the endpoint or the pair as a whole.

SkippedFeatureResponse.description: A pair left without a task.

reason.description: Why its agent cannot run the task.

SkippedItemKindWire.description: The kind of cart item a skip is about. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

SkippedItemResponse.description: The cart item a skip is about.

SkippedPackageResponse.description: A Linux endpoint and package pair a dispatch left out.

detail.description: Human-readable text. It may change between releases.

SkippedUpdateResponse.description: A Windows Update left out because no curated offline package exists for it.

SkippedUserResponse.description: The user whose session a skip is about.

name.description: How the user is named to an operator, when known.

SmartStatusWire.description:
Whether the disk's SMART reliability counter could be read. Treat an
unknown value as unknown.

SnmpAuthProtocolWire.description:
SNMPv3 authentication protocol. `sha1` is for devices that speak nothing
newer.

SnmpSettingsResponse.description:
The SNMP settings of a device. Never a secret: each is `true` once one is
stored.

community_set.description: A v2c community string is stored.

v3_auth_key_set.description: An SNMPv3 authentication key is stored.

v3_priv_key_set.description: An SNMPv3 privacy key is stored.

v3_user.description: The SNMPv3 user name. Null for v2c or when not configured.

oneOf.description: Null: SNMP is not configured.

SnmpVersionWire.description: SNMP version. v1 is not offered.

StalledPackage.description: A winget package whose upstream manifest fetch has given up.

fetch_failure_count.description: Failed fetches so far. Always at or past the give-up threshold.

last_fetch_failure_at.description: Null when no failure time is recorded.

source.description: Where the row came from. Never `custom`: tenant-private uploads are not listed.

version.description: Null when the row carries no version.

StandingWire.description: Where one matching endpoint stands against the app's current version.

StartupItem.description:
One startup item. The write routes take `name`, `item_type` and `source_path`
back as `item_name`, `item_type` and `source_path`.

is_microsoft.description: Signed by Microsoft on Windows, a distribution unit on Linux.

item_type.description:
Where it is registered: `run_key_hklm`, `run_key_hkcu`, `run_once_key_hklm`,
`run_once_key_hkcu`, `startup_folder_allusers`, `startup_folder_user`,
`scheduled_task`, `systemd_unit`, `cron_reboot` or `rc_local`. Treat any
other value as unknown.

signer.description: The executable's signer, when its signature is valid.

source_path.description: The registry key, folder, task path or file it is registered in.

user.description: The user whose profile holds it. Null for an all-users item.

StartupItemsResponse.description:
What starts with the endpoint.

A Linux agent that cannot list its units answers `200` with `{"error": "..."}`
and no `items`.

StopChangeTaskResponse.description: What stopping one task of a Change did.

signalled.description:
Whether the agent was asked to stop the install. `false` for an agent that
does not stream install output, and for one that was offline: only the
queued steps behind the task were cancelled then.

stopped.description: Always `true`: a task that could not be stopped answers an error.

SuccessResponse.description: The body of an action with nothing to return but its outcome.

success.description: Always `true`: a failure answers an error body.

SyncIntervalChangeResponse.description: What a change of the sync interval moved.

SyncIntervalRequest.description: A change of the sync interval.

SyncIntervalWire.description: How often the Bastion is asked for new content, spelled as stored.

TagRequest.description: A tag to create, or the whole of what a tag is changed to.

color.description: `#rrggbb`. Omit it or send null for no colour; on a change that clears it.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters. Unique in the Organization, whatever the case.

color.description: `#rrggbb`. Null when the tag has none, and the console draws its default hue.

endpoint_count.description: How many endpoints carry the tag.

What an action that queues work for an endpoint's agent answers.

The work has not run yet. Read its outcome from
`GET /api/v1/endpoints/{id}/tasks/{task_id}` (`get_endpoint_task`): the
task's `status` leaves `pending` when the agent reports back, and `result`
or `error_message` then carries what happened.

TaskResponse.description: One task queued for, or run by, an endpoint.

deployment_id.description: Set when the task is a step of a deployment.

payload.description:
What the task was asked to do, with secrets removed. Free-form: its keys
depend on `task_type` and are not part of the v1 promise.

result.description: What the agent reported back. Free-form, like `payload`.

tenant_id.description: The Organization that owns the task.

verifies_task_id.description: Set when the task exists to re-measure another task's effect.

TaskStatusWire.description: Where a task stands. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

TaskTypeWire.description: What a task does. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

company_name.description:
The name its surfaces show: the Organization's own, else the
installation's, else `PostureRMM`.

has_logo.description: A logo shows: the Organization's own, else the installation's.

logo_version.description: Changes whenever the logo does. Null when there is none.

TenantListItem.description: An Organization in the list, with its endpoint count.

is_active.description: `false` once the Organization is deactivated: nobody in it can sign in.

parent_tenant_id.description: The MSP that manages this Organization. Null when none does.

settings.description: Free-form Organization settings. Only `branding.company_name` is promised.

TenantTypeWire.description: How an Organization relates to the others. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

error.description: Why it did not. Every secret the channel holds is scrubbed out of it.

success.description: Whether the receiver accepted the test notification.

TrustProvenanceWire.description: How the agent established trust in the server certificate.

UndeliverableWire.description:
Why a Linux package fix cannot be deployed to an endpoint. Treat an unknown
value as unknown.

UninstallAgentRequest.description: Why the agent is being removed, and whether its history goes too.

delete_data.description:
Also delete this endpoint's data once the agent confirms it is gone.
Default `false`.

reason.description: Optional. Recorded in the audit log and passed to the agent.

UnknownAgentResponse.description:
An agent that tried to connect but is not enrolled here.

Everything but `agent_id` and the counters was sent by the connecting agent,
which proved nothing: treat `hostname` and `ip_address` as untrusted text.

hostname.description: What the agent called itself; null when it sent no name.

ip_address.description: The address it connected from; null when unknown.

rejection_reason.description:
Why the last handshake was refused, for example `unknown_agent` or
`revoked_key`. Not a closed set: treat any other value as unknown.

UpdateAlertRuleRequest.description: A change to a rule. A field left out stays as it is.

condition_params.description:
Replaces the whole parameter set (see `POST /alert-rules`): what it
leaves out takes its default. Sending `condition_type` without this
resets the parameters to the new condition's defaults.

endpoint_ids.description: Replaces the endpoint list.

group_ids.description: Replaces the group list.

A change to a catalog entry. A field left out stays as it is. The nullable
ones also take an explicit `null`, which clears them.

A change to an assignment. Absent fields stay as they are. The benchmark

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

never change; send the fields of its own kind only.

pin_version.description: App lines. An explicit `null` clears the pin back to the latest.

products.description: Windows Update lines. They replace the current ones.

entries.description:
The list it ends up holding. It replaces the current one, and the
violations of an application no longer listed go with it.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

UpdateChannelRequest.description: A change to a channel. A field left out stays as it is.

oneOf.description: Changing the type needs `config`, and starts from no secrets.

config.description:
Replaces the whole settings (see `POST /notification-channels`): what it
leaves out is unset, except a secret it leaves out, which keeps the one on
file (when `channel_type` is unchanged). A blank secret is a 422.

UpdateComplianceResultRequest.description: A remediation status to record by hand.

remediation_message.description: A note stored with the status. Ignored without `remediation_status`.

oneOf.description: Where the remediation stands. Without it nothing changes.

UpdateCredentialRequest.description: A change to a credential. The name and username are always replaced.

domain.description: The Windows logon domain. Omitting it clears it.

password.description:
A new secret. Omit it to keep the stored one. Also accepted under the
name `secret`.

oneOf.description: What the new secret is. Defaults to `password`, and needs a new secret.

UpdateDefinitionRequest.description: A change to a definition. A field left out stays as it is.

sections.description: Replaces the whole list: one to 15 sections, in report order.

UpdateEndpointRequest.description: A change to an endpoint. A field left out stays as it is.

group_id.description:
The group to move the endpoint into. An explicit `null` removes it from
its group.

oneOf.description: The metadata the endpoint ends up with.

tag_ids.description: The tags the endpoint ends up with. They replace its current tags.

UpdateFeaturePolicyRequest.description: A change to a feature policy. Absent fields stay as they are.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

items.description: The features it ends up holding. They replace the current ones.

UpdateGroupRequest.description: A change to a group. A field left out stays as it is.

parent_id.description:
The group to move this one under. An explicit `null` moves it to the top
level. A group cannot go under itself or one of its own subgroups.

rules.description:
An object makes the group dynamic with that rule (the shape is on
`POST /groups`). An explicit `null` makes it static and drops the
members the rule had found.

UpdateMaintenanceWindowRequest.description: A change to a maintenance window. Absent fields stay as they are.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

UpdateMonitorRequest.description: A change to a monitor. A field left out stays as it is.

oneOf.description: Replaces the whole auto-fix: what it leaves out is off.

endpoint_ids.description: Replaces the endpoint list.

group_ids.description: Replaces the group list.

UpdatePatchBaselineRequest.description: A change to a baseline's name or description. Absent fields stay as they are.

UpdatePatchPolicyRequest.description: A change to a patch policy. Absent fields stay as they are.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

rules.description: The rules it ends up with. They replace the current ones.

UpdateProfileRequest.description: A field left out stays as it is.

UpdateProxyRequest.description: A change to a proxy. A field left out stays as it is.

UpdateRebootPolicyRequest.description: A change to a reboot policy. Absent fields stay as they are.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

UpdateScanConfigRequest.description: A change to a scan config. A field left out stays as it is.

schedule.description: An explicit `null` (or blank) makes the config manual-only.

UpdateScheduleRequest.description: A change to a schedule. Absent fields stay as they are.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

UpdateScheduledReportRequest.description: A change to a scheduled report. A field left out stays as it is.

recipients.description: Replaces the recipients: at least one.

UpdateScriptRequest.description: A change to a script. A field left out stays as it is.

UpdateTenantRequest.description: A field left out stays as it is.

is_active.description:
`false` deactivates the Organization: every user's sessions and API keys are
revoked and its agents are disconnected.

UpdateUpgradePolicyRequest.description: A change to an upgrade policy. Absent fields stay as they are.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

group_ids.description: The groups it ends up covering. They replace the current ones.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Request body for updating a user. A field left out stays as it is.

is_active.description: `false` deactivates the user and revokes their sessions and API keys.

scope_group_ids.description: Group scope for group-scoped roles. Omit to leave unchanged.

UpgradeChannelWire.description:
The agent release channel an upgrade policy tracks. A request names it, a
response reports it. Treat an unknown value as unknown.

endpoint_ids.description: The endpoints it covers.

group_ids.description:
The groups it covers. With no endpoints either, it covers the whole
Organization.

tag_ids.description: The tags it covers. Read-only here: this API does not write them.

UpgradeRequest.description: The agent release to move to.

target_version.description:
A version the install holds a release for, for example `1.15.0`. Any
other value answers `400`.

UpgradeResponse.description: An upgrade queued, with the deployment that tracks it.

deployment_id.description: The deployment that records the upgrade.

UploadRequest.description: The fields of an upload, as the page's dialog sends them.

detect_name.description:
The name the app shows in Installed apps. Required for the first upload of
an EXE or MSIX app, so endpoints running it can be offered updates.

file.description:
The installer: `.msi`, `.exe` or `.msix`, 4 KB to 500 MB. Its extension and
its first bytes must match `installer_type`.

install_timeout.description: Whole minutes from 1 to 1440. Blank is the default.

name.description:
The app's name. A new app only; the next version of an app takes its name.
An app named like an existing one is that app's next version.

silent_args.description:
What a blank value does depends on the type: an MSI is installed with
`/qn /norestart`; an EXE with no arguments is stopped after 120 seconds, so
give it its silent switches; MSIX ignores it.

uninstall_command.description: Run to remove this version. Blank uses the uninstaller the app registers.

oneOf.description:
The detection rule this upload set. Null when the app already had one and
the upload left it.

signer.description: Who signed the installer, when its signature could be read.

UpsertPinBody.description: The version to pin a profile to.

pinned_version.description: The profile version to follow. Must not be empty.

reason.description: Why. Kept with the pin and in the audit log.

UserDetailResponse.description: One user, with the fields only an administrator sees.

is_bootstrap.description: The install's first administrator: its role cannot change and it cannot be deleted.

locked_until.description: Null when the account is not locked.

must_change_password.description: The user must choose a new password at the next sign-in.

oneOf.description:
Present **only** on a `PATCH` that deactivated this user: what happened
to their live remote sessions (#2326).

It is a *report*, not a status: deactivation is durable before this runs,
so a non-zero `failed` still comes back on a 200. The caller is being
told that the account is off but that a socket teardown did not record
cleanly — go read the audit log — and is emphatically **not** being
invited to retry the deactivation.

scope_group_ids.description: The groups a group-scoped role reads. Absent for a role that reads everything.

is_bootstrap.description: The install's first administrator: its role cannot change and it cannot be deleted.

scope_group_ids.description: The groups a group-scoped role reads. Absent for a role that reads everything.

UserPermissionsResponse.description: A user's add-on permissions, one entry per permission.

UserProfileResponse.description: The signed-in user, in the Organization the request acts in.

role.description: The role in the acting Organization.

scope_group_ids.description: The groups a group-scoped role reads. Absent for a role that reads everything.

tenant_name.description: The acting Organization's name. Absent on the answer to `PATCH`.

oneOf.description: Absent on the answer to `PATCH`.

totp_enabled.description: Whether the user has two-factor sign-in enrolled.

ViolationResponse.description: An open violation: a banned application installed on an endpoint.

auto_removable.description:
Whether the application can be removed silently. When it cannot, a
person has to remove it on the endpoint.

VulnerabilitySeverityWire.description:
A vulnerability's severity bucket. `none` is a real CVSS 0.0; `unscored` is a
CVE the NVD has not scored yet.

VulnerabilityStatusWire.description: Lifecycle of one vulnerability on one endpoint.

oneOf.description: Now.
At a wall-clock time in a time zone.

timezone.description:
An IANA name such as `Europe/London`, or `endpoint_local` for each
endpoint's own reported zone (UTC where it reports none).

oneOf.description: When each endpoint next enters its maintenance window.

WindowsUpdateResponse.description: One Windows update and where it stands on one endpoint.

pending_work.description:
Whether the update belongs in the endpoint's pending queue: not
superseded here and not a SQL Server cumulative-update alternative.

scan_catalog_version.description: The `wsusscn2.cab` version an offline scan ran against.

scan_source.description:
How the row was discovered: null for an online scan, `offline_cab` for a
scan against a `wsusscn2.cab`.

status.description: The update's state on this endpoint. Treat a value you do not know as unknown.

WsTransportWire.description: The agent's own report of its WebSocket state.

bearer.description: An API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer frt_...`. The key's role ceiling and group scope bound every call. A key minted in a client Organization acts there; otherwise `X-Tenant-Id` selects among the Organizations the key may act in.
